visual_text: Who gets left out
Lecanemab, a new Alzheimer's drug: Swedish primary care study
Who meets the criteria for lecanemab?
607 people seeing a GP with memory symptoms, any cause
86 met lecanemab criteria after full tests: about 1 in 7
About 1 in 6
on a blood thinner
About 1 in 4
with marked small-vessel changes on MRI
Reasons overlap; most had more than one
Alasdair MacLullich
Borgström Bolmsjö et al., Alzheimer's Res Ther 2026
Who gets left out
Would they have been in the trial?
237 older people with early memory problems and amyloid (US)
112 met the trial's inclusion rules
19 remained after exclusions: about 8 in 100
Frail people only, in a separate study: 4 of 44 met the trial's rules
In a separate study of 120 pre-frail and frail people with amyloid: 1 in 5 met the trial's rules, about half met clinic-use recommendations
Alasdair MacLullich
Pittock et al., Neurology 2023; Bellelli et al., Alzheimer's Res Ther 2026
alt_text: Funnel: 607 people seeing a GP in Sweden with memory symptoms narrowing to 86 who met lecanemab criteria after full tests, about 1 in 7. Two separate boxes: about 1 in 6 on a blood thinner, about 1 in 4 with marked small-vessel changes on MRI. Reasons overlap.

Three bars scaled to count: 237 older people with early memory problems and amyloid, 112 meeting inclusion rules, 19 remaining after exclusions, about 8 in 100. Below, 44 squares with 4 filled: frail people meeting trial rules, from a separate study of 120.
